title: Sr Cyber Engineer
description: Our Mission Our mission is to SAVE AND IMPROVE LIVES BY EMPOWERING HEALTHCARE CONSUMERS. Come be part of remarkable. Overview How you can make a difference HealthEquity is expanding its use of AI. Teammates use generative AI tools, teams are building applications on large language models, and AI agents are beginning to connect to internal systems and data. These uses bring risks that existing controls were not designed for, including prompt injection, sensitive data leaving through prompts and tool calls, and agents operating with more access than they need. This role builds HealthEquity 's defenses for these use cases on two of our core security platforms, Cloudflare and Palo Alto Networks. It also owns core engineering for both platforms, because AI controls depend on the edge, network, and access layers beneath them. This is a hands-on engineering role. You will design, build, deploy, and operate these controls yourself, and you will be accountable for how they perform in production. What you’ll be doing Build defenses for AI use cases Discover and govern AI use. Build visibility into the AI applications, coding assistants, agents, and MCP servers in use across HealthEquity , including unsanctioned tools. Apply allow, monitor, isolate, or block policies based on application risk and data sensitivity. Protect member data in AI interactions. Design and tune data loss prevention for prompts, file uploads, responses, and agent tool calls so member PHI, PII, and financial data reach only approved AI services, without blocking legitimate work. Protect HealthEquity -built AI applications. Deploy runtime protections for production AI applications and agents, including prompt injection and jailbreak detection, sensitive data detection, topic and output controls, token-based rate limiting, and audit logging that protects the sensitive data it captures. Secure agent access to internal systems. Define how AI agents authenticate, which tools and data they can reach, and how each tool call is logged and attributed to a person or service. Route approved MCP servers through governed access paths and block connections that bypass them. Centralize access to AI models. Route LLM provider traffic through managed AI gateways for policy enforcement, usage and cost visibility, and credential protection. Provider API keys live in a secrets vault, never in source code, configuration files, or pipelines. Handle AI agents on member-facing sites. Work with product and fraud prevention teams to decide how member and employer sites and APIs treat AI crawlers and agents acting on a person's behalf, then enforce that decision with Cloudflare bot controls. Test what you build. Run adversarial testing against AI applications and agents, covering prompt injection, data exfiltration, tool misuse, and privilege abuse, and turn findings into control and detection improvements. title: Senior Marketing Manager - Narrative and Launch
description: Senior Marketing Manager - Narrative and Launch US Remote · Reports to SVP Marketing AI is hitting a limit. Not in the models, not in the data, not in the software. It's a power limit, and it lives in the chip, where the physics is fixed and you can only squeeze so many bits out of a watt. Every watt AI wants comes off the same grid everyone else shares. The problem isn't unknown. The rest of the industry is trying to solve it by making the same chip better, which earns incremental gains, not the step change that puts AI everywhere without breaking the grid. EnCharge AI is using a different set of physics: analog in-memory computing, which computes with charge instead of switching transistors, built and running at roughly 20x the performance per watt. Why this role exists This role is strategy and execution in the same seat, with the balance tilted toward execution. It helps shape how a genuinely hard technology gets understood, and it spends most of its days doing the hands-on work that makes that happen. That combination is hard to hold, and rewarding for the person who can. Analog compute has been the industry's white whale. For decades it's been the thing everyone agreed would change computing, if anyone could get it to work at scale. We have. Now it has to be understood, by developers, by the companies building the devices, by the analysts shaping the category, and by an industry with a lot invested in the current answer. Hard technology does not explain itself, and the companies that win this category will be the ones people can follow. Marketing is a small team, and this role reports to the SVP of Marketing. It drives the launches, plays a central role in developing the brand, corporate, and product narrative, and reaches into everything else a small team has to cover. What you'll drive Launches. You drive them: the plan, the sequencing, the proof points, and the readiness of everyone who has to talk about it. That means hands-on execution as well as coordinating digital marketing, PR, and events into one coherent multichannel launch. The narrative. How we explain what we've built, to each audience that matters, in a way that survives contact with a skeptical one. The SVP of Marketing owns the brand, corporate, and product narrative, and you're a key player in building it: you research, build, test, and bring the evidence that changes it, then make it hold everywhere it has to work: the site, the deck, the brief, the booth, the briefing, the field. Execution. You'll get your hands dirty: content, social, creative, events. And you'll coordinate the vendors and freelancers who extend what a small team can do and hold their work to the standard. Translating the technology. You work directly with the people who built this and turn it into explainers, technical briefs, launch narratives, and customer stories. You are not the deepest technical mind in the room. You are the person who knows which question unlocks the explanation, and what to do w

Edge is our heavy hitter when all else fails. It runs a Rust peer runtime on residential Windows PCs that long-polls our command-and-control service over mTLS gRPC, making fetches look indistinguishable from real human traffic using genuine hardware, residential IPs, and seamless fingerprints. Our Edge Platform squad manages both the control plane and data plane of this stack. Right now, we’re expanding from Windows into Android devices on mobile networks and self-hosted Linux (with macOS on the horizon). Mobile is where our biggest opportunity lies: websites that block desktop traffic often welcome a real mobile phone on a 4G connection. That’s where you come in! You’ll be the lead engineer making our peer run smoothly and invisibly across every platform—binding Rust to native network stacks and OS APIs via FFI, and turning scattered devices into a well-oiled, observable fleet. We’re a lean, senior team, so you’ll collaborate closely with our Team Lead, Principal Engineer, and the Browser Stack and Antiban squads. Requirements What You’ll Be Doing Build our cross-platform peer runtime: Take ownership of the Rust peer binary across Windows, Android, Linux (and eventually macOS)—handling process lifecycles, background tasks, networking, automatic updates, and rock-solid stability on unmanaged hardware. title: Training Specialist - Remote
description: You're not running a classroom. You're building the EAs our clients count on, one person at a time. Why does this role exist? You're an in-house Magic employee, full-time from day one, and not a freelance or client-placed role. Every EA who steps in front of a client has to be ready, not "probably ready," actually ready. That's what you're here for. You run the sessions that turn new hires into confident, capable Executive Assistants, and you're the one who calls it when someone is or isn't there yet. This isn't about lecturing from a slide deck. You're facilitating, assessing, coaching, and constantly tightening the program itself because "how we've always done it" isn't good enough if it's not producing EAs who can hold their own with US clients. You'll work closely with the Assistant Training Manager, but the day-to-day judgment calls, including how a session goes, whether someone's ready for their mock client call, and what feedback actually lands, are yours. What Winning Looks Like You run daily virtual sessions that trainees rate as clear, engaging, and genuinely useful, not just "completed." You grade every assessment against the rubric, not your gut, and your calls hold up under review. You synthesize checkpoint scores, mock interviews, and day-to-day notes into a readiness call that's right more often than not. You flag performance risks and program gaps early before they become a trainee's problem in front of a client. You ship at least one program improvement a quarter that measurably moves engagement or retention. What You'll Actually Do Training Facilitation Trainee Readiness You lead daily, trainer-led virtual sessions for each assigned batch, and you keep every scrap of training documentation accurate and current. You run rubric-based assessments at each stage of the program, graded on defined criteria, not impression, and you resolve trainee questions and concerns as they come up, on the spot. EA Assessment Coaching You run mock client intro calls and mock interviews to pressure-test readiness beyond checkpoint scores, then pull all of it, such as checkpoints, mock performance, and facilitation notes, into one clear readiness read per trainee. You coach on presentation, communication, and the mental shift from "doing tasks" to "providing strategic support," and you call out each trainee's specific strengths and gaps with targeted next steps. Program Design Improvement You work with the Assistant Training Manager to review what's working and what isn't, then build the agreed-upon fixes, including content, structure, and delivery. You design simulations and role-play scenarios that mirror the real situations EAs actually run into with clients. Coordination Reporting You keep the Assistant Training Manager and Training Supervisor looped in on trainee progress and project status in real time, and you flag roadblocks before they become missed deadlines. You escalate unresolved issues or performance risks to the right person — Superviso

We also use these images in our local development environment allowing coding locally against all of our services. We have a well-documented public API that is consumed by our front-end JavaScript app as well as numerous integrations. Our infrastructure is heavily automated using Terraform, Ansible and other AWS tools. We love open sourcing our code and ideas on our GitHub and on The Making of Close , our behind-the-scenes Product & Engineering blog. Check out our open source projects like SocketShark , TaskTiger , LimitLion and ciso8601 . AI is both how we build and what we ship, and that's reshaped what engineering looks like. This is a transformation we’re embracing and find deeply exciting. About the Role Close runs on Python: Flask web apps, TaskTiger, billions of MongoDB documents, a public REST API that customers and external agents both build on. Four product teams ship features on top of that every week. Backend Platform owns the foundation underneath it all. As an Engineer on our Backend Platform team, you’re building for other engineers.
